topic: How the engine feels on track
statement: The Beta RX 450 engine makes its best power in the midrange and feels heavy and slow to rev, more like a tractor than a screamer. It is quicker than it feels. Short-shifting and riding it a gear high works better than revving it out. On the dyno the standard map (sun icon) made 57.8 hp near 9,900 rpm and about 34.8 lb-ft near 7,400 rpm; it matched the class leader from 6,000 to 7,000 rpm and fell behind above about 8,000 rpm. The soft map (rain cloud icon) made 53.7 hp and 32.8 lb-ft.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Maps, map switch and throttle cams
statement: The RX 450 has two maps: standard (sun icon) and soft (rain cloud icon). Testers found the soft map ran cleaner but was too slow to race and only worth using on hard, slick tracks. The map switch sits in the handlebar pad; the bike comes with a bracket to move it to the handlebar. Four extra throttle cams come with the bike, from quick-turn to slow-turn; testers preferred the quick-turn cam (black, marked 44).
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Rev limiter cuts abruptly and throttle blips can cut the ignition
statement: The RX 450 rev limiter comes in at about 11,100 rpm and feels like a flutter or cut rather than a soft fade. Testers first thought it was an electrical fault. Quick throttle blips can also chirp or cut the ignition. This is how the bike is mapped, not a broken part. An aftermarket full exhaust added power but did not remove the limiter. Fix on track: shift earlier and keep it in the midrange.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Flame-outs and stalling at low rpm
statement: Testers reported the RX 450 flaming out and stalling at low rpm, mostly in tight or trail-speed riding. Beta fitted a stronger battery for 2025 but the stalling was still there in testing. No fix was confirmed in the tests. If yours stalls, first rule out the basics (idle speed, battery charge and terminals, fuel quality) and then ask the dealer about mapping updates.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Cam chain tensioner can over-tension
statement: The RX 450 uses a hydraulic cam chain tensioner that can over-tension the chain. Beta sells a manual tensioner as an alternative. Testers reset the tensioner and found the engine felt slightly freer afterward, with no big change in character. Follow the owner's manual procedure for the reset.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Stock suspension behaviour (2024)
statement: Stock 2024 RX 450 suspension was the testers' biggest complaint. The KYB 48 mm fork felt stiff at the top of the stroke and soft deeper in: it rode high and harsh until the front brake or a big hit, then dove and could nearly bottom. The shock felt plush at the top and stiff in the middle. What helped: adding 20 cc of oil per fork leg for bottoming resistance, softening compression, and slowing rebound. Beta's own suspension department supplied a revalve that balanced the bike much better.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Stock suspension behaviour and tested settings (2025)
statement: For 2025 Beta kept the RX 450 spring rates and changed the KYB valving at both ends. Testers still found the fork too soft at the top: it dives under braking and leaves the rider in the harsh part of the stroke. Tested setup: add 10 cc of oil per fork leg, fork tubes 2 mm up in the clamps, rear sag 102 to 105 mm. The test did not publish clicker numbers.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Handling and turning
statement: The RX 450 is hard to start into a corner but steers well once it is leaned in. Engine braking is light in 2nd and 3rd gear; dropping a gear adds engine braking, loads the front tyre and makes it turn sharper, at the cost of a harsher fork. At high rpm and full throttle the chassis feels like it binds up. Testers tried aftermarket triple clamps with 20.5 mm offset (stock is 22 mm): shorter wheelbase, less trail, a more connected front end and better bump comfort. With those clamps some riders went to 110 mm of sag to calm the steering.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Ergonomics: tall, wide tank, thin seat
statement: The RX 450 sits tall and is hard for shorter riders to get a foot down. The steering head is high and the bars are flat with little sweep. The fuel tank is wide at the front and pushes the knees out. The seat is flat with thin foam; adding foam helps comfort but raises the seat. The stock grips are thick in the middle and can blister the thumb.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Weight as tested and what it is built from
statement: The RX 450 weighed 239 lb on the test scale with no fuel and all other fluids. Engine: 450 cc four-stroke, 5-speed, four valves, finger followers, twin cams, 46 mm throttle body, stainless exhaust. Chromoly steel frame. KYB 48 mm closed-cartridge spring fork and KYB 50 mm shock. Nissin brakes. Hydraulic clutch with a single Belleville (diaphragm) spring that has three preload settings to change lever feel. Tool-less airbox cover.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: What changed for 2025
statement: 2025 RX 450 changes from 2024: revised KYB valving front and rear (spring rates unchanged); updated mapping; sharper footpegs; rubber-mounted bar clamps with the bars 5 mm higher; stronger battery; rear sprocket changed from the two-material 50-tooth to an all-aluminium 51-tooth; rear axle up from 20 mm to 22 mm; reinforced subframe; front fender and number plate changed from blue to red.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Oil changes: two separate oil compartments
statement: The RX 450 keeps engine oil and gearbox/clutch oil in two separate compartments, so an oil change means two drains and two fills. Use the quantities and grades in the owner's manual for each side. The shock can be removed without lifting the subframe: take the muffler off, then the shock bolts.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Small parts that wore or came loose in testing
statement: Reported in testing: the 2024 footpegs were not sharp and wore fast (changed for 2025); a muffler guard bolt went missing; the handlebar pad cover peeled on the first day. Check the muffler guard bolts with the rest of your pre-ride bolt check.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: How the engine feels on track (2021-2024 engine)
statement: The 2021 RX 300 engine feels like a strong 250 two-stroke rather than a hard-hitting 300: it builds smoothly, does not fade quickly and does not get away from the rider. Two maps on a bar-pad switch: sun for loamy, grippy dirt and rain for slick dirt. The rain map softens the first part of the throttle and then revs long and linear. Factory jetting was right as delivered; on a cool morning testers opened the air screw half a turn.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Power valve (BPV) adjustment
statement: The RX 300 power valve preload is adjusted with an Allen key on the left side of the engine. Tested settings on the 2021 bike: 1 to 1-1/2 turns in from fully out worked best for most riders; fast riders on high-speed tracks liked about half a turn in from fully out. Change it a quarter to half a turn at a time. Different power valve springs are available from Beta.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Tested motocross settings (2021, KYB fork and Sachs shock)
statement: Race settings the testers arrived at on the 2021 RX 300. Fork (KYB 48 mm, 4.5 N/mm springs): add 30 cc of oil per leg, compression all the way in (stock 8 clicks out), rebound 9 clicks out (stock 8), fork height at the first line. Shock (Sachs, 52 N/mm spring; riders over 180 lb use 54 N/mm): high-speed compression 3 clicks out (stock 20), low-speed compression 18 clicks out (stock 22), rebound 11 clicks out (stock 15), rear sag 110 mm (stock 105 mm). The stock fork was far too soft for motocross, which is why the compression ended up fully closed; a revalve is the real fix.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Handling (2021)
statement: The 2021 RX 300 turns in well but wants to stand up mid-corner unless the rider sits about an inch further forward than feels natural. It feels rear-heavy and is hard to rotate in the air. Adding fork oil improved straight-line stability. The stock shock sits high: at 105 mm of sag tall riders were still on their toes, and 110 mm worked better. The seat is tall and flat and the 2.5-gallon tank is wide.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Spoke next to the rim lock loosens; fender rub
statement: On the 2021 RX 300 the spoke beside the rim lock came loose on every outing; testers used medium threadlocker on that nipple. Check spokes after every ride. The front fender can touch the front tyre on hard hits and make noise. The shock rebound clicker cannot be reached with the bike on a stand.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: What changed for 2025
statement: 2025 RX 300 changes: new chromoly frame with a main spar 10 mm wider, based on the RX 450; lighter aluminium subframe; KYB fork with revised settings and more travel; larger-body KYB shock (the earlier bike used a Sachs shock); revised cylinder porting and a higher-compression head (13.3:1); new motocross 5-speed gearbox; stiffer clutch diaphragm spring; new pipe and shorter silencer; smaller, lighter front caliper; narrower radiators; bars 5 mm higher on vibration-damping mounts; smaller 1.8-gallon tank; tool-less airbox.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: How the engine feels on track (2025)
statement: The 2025 RX 300 has strong low-to-mid power and crisp throttle: third gear can be carried through corners with little clutch. It goes flat on top and does not pull far into over-rev, so short-shift it. Map 1 (sun) is snappier down low; map 2 (rain) is softer at first and pulls longer.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Jetting: rich off the bottom, air screw fix (2025)
statement: As delivered the 2025 RX 300 was slightly rich at small throttle openings and when going from closed to open throttle. Turning the air screw out to 1.5 turns cleaned it up and sharpened response. The tester needed no other jetting change at their tracks.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Tested settings from stock (2025, 175-180 lb rider)
statement: Stock 2025 RX 300 suspension is balanced and smooth but a little soft under load, with some front-to-rear pitching at speed. Changes a 175-180 lb tester made from the stock clickers: shock low-speed compression 3 clicks stiffer, shock rebound 2 clicks slower, shock high-speed compression a quarter turn in; fork compression 2 clicks stiffer and fork rebound 2 clicks slower. That calmed the busy feeling.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Ergonomics and feel (2025)
statement: The 2025 RX 300 is slim and comfortable for a rider around 5 ft 11 in. The stock handlebar is wide and straight; trimming a few millimetres off each end helps. The side panels are narrow, which makes the bike harder to squeeze with the legs in the air. Tested weight 219 lb without fuel.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: How the engine feels on track
statement: The Desmo450 MX has strong torque from low rpm and a smooth build all the way through. There is no sharp drop at the rev limiter: it carries cleanly into the next gear. Second gear feels long, with strong bottom end and over-rev; second suits tight corners and third suits fast sweepers.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Gearing as tested
statement: The test bike ran 13/49 final gearing. Note that Ducati's own specification page lists 13/51, so count the teeth on your bike. The tester felt second gear was long for tight corners and would try 13/52 before changing the front sprocket. A factory rider's bike at the launch ran 14/51 with an aftermarket exhaust and other changes.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Tested sag and clicker changes
statement: The Showa 48 mm coil fork and linkage Showa shock are a little firmer than most production 450s. At 102 mm of rear sag the front felt overloaded and dove off the throttle. Going to 105 mm of sag and 2 clicks stiffer on compression at both ends balanced it. The tester noted that 3 mm of sag makes a clear difference on this bike.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Maps, traction control and quickshifter in use
statement: Two maps: standard and aggressive, with more tuning through Ducati's app. Traction control worked well on hard-pack and loose-over-hard corners, even on the aggressive map. A quick flick of the clutch lever turns traction control off for a few seconds. The up-only quickshifter works but is a matter of taste.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Handling, brakes and ergonomics
statement: The Desmo450 MX feels light and easy to move, and stays planted under braking and through chop. Brembo brakes on 260 mm front and 240 mm rear discs were a highlight. Rider position is neutral on the pegs. The seat has a deep dip that makes it harder for taller riders to slide forward out of corners. Tyres as delivered: 80/100-21 front and 110/90-19 rear; the tester wanted to try a 120 rear on hard-pack.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: How the engine and electronic power valve feel
statement: The 2014 CX65 has a strong bottom-end hit and pulls well through the range, with a clear surge when the power valve opens. The power valve is electronic: it opens at 8,500 rpm and goes from closed to open in about 30 milliseconds. Six-speed gearbox, one down and five up.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Gearing and clutch as tested
statement: The 2014 CX65 test bike ran 14/45 gearing, which suited most tracks. Add one tooth to the rear for tight tracks or newer riders. The hydraulic clutch has a quick-change cover and can take an extra drive and friction plate for more grip. Smaller riders found the lever pull tiring in long motos.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Suspension layout and behaviour
statement: 2014 CX65: 37 mm fork with 220 mm of travel, rebound and compression clickers on the left leg and a bottoming adjuster on the right leg. Rear shock with no linkage, 270 mm of travel, with rebound plus high-speed and low-speed compression adjusters. It soaks up small chop and takes hard landings, and young test riders needed only small clicker changes. The test did not publish click numbers.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Rear brake pedal is flimsy; front brake feel
statement: On the 2014 CX65 the rear brake pedal is large and bends easily; fit a brake snake (a cable from the pedal tip to the frame) so a rut or crash does not fold it. The front brake (205 mm disc, four-piston caliper) is strong but less progressive than rivals; set the lever reach and the freeplay dial to suit small hands. The caliper sits about 2 mm from the spokes, so keep the wheel true. The fuel tank is wide for taller kids moving forward.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: How the engine and clutch feel
statement: The 2016 CX50 SR hits hard for a 50 and is a lot for a first-time rider. With one gear it spends much of the lap near peak rpm; power flattens around 15,000 rpm. The three-shoe automatic clutch should engage at about 7,200 rpm.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Reading clutch engagement rpm
statement: On the 2016 CX50 SR, fit a tachometer hour meter and watch where the clutch grabs. Engaging below about 7,200 rpm points to a weak spring stack (lost tension). Engaging above about 7,200 rpm points to the clutch slipping. Clean debris out of the clutch spring stacks through the side ports. Use the spring stack arrangement in the owner's manual as the baseline.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Friction drive (CFD) torque checks and service rhythm
statement: The CX50 SR friction drive (CFD) protects the crank, gearbox, clutch and chain, and it needs checking: check its torque at 2 hours on a new bike, then about every 4 hours once the bike has 8 hours on it. The long-term tester almost always found it needed tightening. A slipping CFD takes away the hit and the protection. Job: drain the oil, remove the side case, torque to the manual figure, and clean the spring stacks with contact or carb cleaner. Change the oil every couple of hours. Re-grease the steering head bearings around 25 hours and replace around 50 hours.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: Handling, bars and brakes
statement: The 2016 CX50 SR turns well in ruts and berms and stays stable on straights. For fast or sandy tracks, lower the fork tubes in the clamps (raise the front) to stop the front tucking. The stock bar bend sweeps back too far for many kids; there are two bar mount positions for growing riders. The footpegs are narrow; wider ones are available. The brakes have good feel but are hard to bleed; the tester saw about 65 to 75 hard hours from them.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.

topic: What changed for 2016
statement: 2016 CX50 SR changes: new rear shock with Allen-screw high-speed and low-speed compression adjusters (2015 used a large nut for high-speed); improved fork with new seals and wipers for smoother first travel; better steering head seals; better clutch cover sealing; black anodised wheels. Fork: 32 mm upside-down cartridge fork, 210 mm travel, with compression, rebound and bottoming adjusters.
notes: From a published track test of this bike. One test crew's result on their tracks; use it as a starting point and confirm against the owner's manual.
